messages.subject: 3 charts among each other
parts:
Dear ggplot Users,

at the moment I am writing a term paper to the topic "Company scandals and stock prices - an Event Study Analysis using the example of MLP AG".
I would like to plot 3 charts among each other, unfortunately it does not work:(
Could you please help and advise me, which instruction I must give to R / ggplot, so that I can get 3 charts among each other.
Another alternative would be, to scaling down the y axis. Do you know the instruction for that?

These are my instructions for the 3 charts so far (they work, but they are too big in my opinion):

Sehr geehrter Herr Richter,
ich studiere an der FOM in Dortmund und schreibe zur Zeit eine Seminararbeit im Fach Empirisches Finance & Accounting. Mein Thema: Unternehmensskandale und Aktienkurse - eine Event Study Analysis am Beispiel der MLP AG.
Ich möchte gerne in meiner Seminararbeit 3 Grafiken (untereinander!) zeigen. Mir wurde ggplot2 empfohlen und meine Befehle lauten wie folgt:
# 1. Graph zeichnen --> kumulierte Renditen im SchÃ¤tzfenster

ggplot(data=schaetz, aes(x=Datum)) + geom_line(aes(y=KumulierteRendite_MLP, col ="blue")) +
geom_line(aes(y=KumulierteRendite_BM, col="red")) +
ylab("Kumulierte Rendite") +
xlab("Monat") +
ggtitle("kumulierte Renditen im SchÃ¤tzfenster Mai 2001 bis Mai 2002") +
scale_colour_manual(name = 'Werte', values =c('blue'='blue','red'='red'), labels = c('MLP','CDAX'))
scale_x_date(breaks = c(event_day, event$Datum[15], event$Datum[30] ))

# 2. Graph zeichnen -- > kumulierte Renditen im Eventfenster

ggplot(data=event, aes(x=Datum)) + geom_line(aes(y=KumulierteRendite_MLP, col ="blue")) +
geom_line(aes(y=KumulierteRendite_BM, col="red")) +
ylab("Kumulierte Rendite") +
xlab("Monat") +
ggtitle("kumulierte Renditen im Eventfenster Mai 2002 - Juli 2002 ") +
geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(event_day), col="green") +

# 3. Graph zeichnen --> abnormale Rendite im Eventfenster

ggplot(data=event, aes(x=Datum)) + geom_line(aes(y=AbnormaleRendite, col ="blue")) +
ylab("abnormale Rendite") +
xlab("Monat") +
ggtitle("abnormale Renditen im Eventfenster Mai 2002 - Juli 2002 ") +
geom_vline(xintercept = as.numeric(event_day), col="green") +
scale_colour_manual(name = 'Werte', values =c('blue'='blue','red'='red'), labels = c('MLP','CDAX'))
scale_x_date(breaks = c(event_day, event$Datum[15], event$Datum[30] ))

Thanks in advance for your help.

Regards
Corinna

messages.subject: Re: 3 charts among each other
parts:
>I would like to plot 3 charts among each other, unfortunately it does not
>work:(

I'm afraid something has been lost in translation here, I don't understand
what you mean by 3 charts among each other. (Not intending to be critical,
I can't even imagine being able to ask a question like this outside my
first language).

Do you want the three charts side by side? In a column? Or a single chart
with the three types of information indicated?

>Another alternative would be, to scaling down the y axis. Do you know the
>instruction for that?

Without having an example dataset, it is hard to be much help. Can you
share your data with us? Or a small example set which would enable people
to draw graphs like those you want (and use your provided code as a guide)?

I suspect you need to get your data into long format (e.g. Using melt from
library reshape2) so that all the observations are in a single column with
the identifying factors in other columns (date, variable, type of variable
‹ MLP, abnormal, CDAX) then plot it with a facet_wrap to get a column or
row of graphs maybe with the scale option set in facet_wrap. But without
data and a clear description of what you want to achieve, I think that is
about as far as I can go.

>These are my instructions for the 3 charts so far (they work, but they
>are too big in my opinion):

The charts are too big? You should set this when opening the device you
want to save them to. For example, use ggplot to create a ggplot object

my.plot <- ggplot(DF)+geom_line(aes(x=d,y=v))
pdf("myplot.pdf",height=3,width=7) # to save to pdf 3 inches high, 7 wide
print(my.plot) # print your ggplot object to the device
dev.off() # close the device

You might find you then need to have a couple of attempts tweaking font
sizes etc in your ggplot object with theme(). See ?theme

Regards,
Ron.
